belongs_to: 3.1 Proportionality - A Quick Recap: 'we can use the cross-multiplication method' for 6 : 3 and 4 : 2 (Viswanath's and Puneet's idli batter)
description: Small centred diagram on white background. Two ratios on one horizontal line: '6 : 3' on the left and '4 : 2' on the right (plain dark serif text, gap between them). A blue (teal-blue) arc ABOVE them is a half-ellipse/semicircle whose left foot ends just above the '6' (left end of '6 : 3') and whose right foot ends just above the '2' (right end of '4 : 2'): it joins 6 and 2. A small red '×' sits above the middle of this top arc. A second blue arc BELOW them is a smaller U-shape whose left foot starts just below the '3' (right end of '6 : 3') and whose right foot ends just below the '4' (left end of '4 : 2'): it joins 3 and 4. No other text, no numbers for the products (the products are written in the sentence below the figure: 'The two products are the same (12)').

belongs_to: 3.2 Ratios in Maps: 'Using the map above, can you find the geographical distance between Bengaluru and Chennai? Also ... Mangaluru and Chennai' (Hint: use a ruler); also the explanation of RF 1 : 60,00,000
description: Full-width rectangular coloured physical map of South India (land in beige/cream with green hills and faint road lines, sea in light blue), with a thin black frame. GRATICULE LABELS: top edge and bottom edge, 8 longitude labels each: 72°E, 74°E, 76°E, 78°E, 80°E, 82°E, 84°E, 86°E (left to right); left edge and right edge, 6 latitude labels each (top to bottom): 18°N, 16°N, 14°N, 12°N, 10°N, 8°N (the labels are written rotated 90 degrees on both side edges). CITY MARKERS: exactly 13 cities, each a red dot with a white/black ring, name in bold black serif text next to the dot (name below the dot in every case). Approximate position (longitude, latitude, estimated from the axis labels): Hyderabad (about 78.5°E, 17.3°N, top centre); Vishakapatnam (printed with this spelling, about 83.2°E, 17.7°N, top right near the coast, label below-left of its dot); Tirupati (about 79.4°E, 13.6°N); Chennai (about 80.3°E, 13.1°N, on the east coast just right-below Tirupati); Bengaluru (about 77.6°E, 12.9°N, inland, west of Chennai); Mangaluru (about 74.8°E, 12.8°N, on the west coast); Mysuru (about 76.6°E, 12.3°N); Kannur (about 75.4°E, 11.9°N, west coast just below Mangaluru); Puducherry (about 79.8°E, 11.9°N, east coast); Coimbatore (about 76.9°E, 11.0°N); Kochi (about 76.2°E, 9.9°N, west coast); Madurai (about 78.1°E, 9.9°N); Thiruvananthapuram (about 76.9°E, 8.5°N, southern tip, label sits on the bottom edge). WATER LABELS: 'A R A B I A N' on the first line and 'S E A' on the second line (letter-spaced, blue italic bold) in the sea at left; 'B A Y  O F' and 'B E N G A L' on two lines (blue italic bold) in the sea at right. A tip of Sri Lanka is visible at the bottom right (south-east). COMPASS ROSE: top right corner, black four-point star with grey secondary points, letters N (top), S (bottom), E (right), W (left). LEGEND: right side of the map, the word 'LEGEND' in letter-spaced bold capitals, below it a red dot with ring followed by 'CITY'. SCALE TEXT: bottom right inside the map, bold letter-spaced text 'RF = 1 : 60,00,000'. Bottom left inside the map in small italic text: 'Map not to scale'. No scale bar and no distance gridlines are printed.
unclear: City dot positions are read off the picture and given only as approximate longitude/latitude (about +/-0.2 degrees).
A distance read with a ruler depends on the printed size on paper; the scanned picture has no scale bar, so distances cannot be measured exactly from the image.

belongs_to: Example 3: 'For some construction, 110 units of concrete are needed. How many units of cement, sand, and gravel are needed if these are to be mixed in the ratio 1 : 1.5 : 3?' (picture after '1 x 20 = 20 units of cement, 1.5 x 20 = 30 units of sand, and 3 x 20 = 60 units of gravel')
description: Illustrated diagram on a pale cream rounded-rectangle background. TOP CENTRE: one dark grey-brown heap of concrete mix, with the bold black sans-serif label '110 units of concrete' directly below it. From just below that label THREE black arrows fan out downwards: left arrow points down-left, middle arrow points straight down, right arrow points down-right. Small bold labels at the arrow tips: '1' below-left of the left arrowhead, '1.5' below the middle arrowhead, '3' below-left of the right arrowhead. BOTTOM ROW, three heaps side by side, left to right: (1) a pale grey-white heap of cement, label '20 units of cement'; (2) an orange-brown heap of sand, label '30 units of sand'; (3) a heap of grey stones (gravel) with a few loose stones scattered around it, label '60 units of gravel'. Each bottom label is bold black sans-serif, placed under its heap. Heaps are all drawn the same size (not scaled to the quantities).
unclear: The three heaps are equal in size in the picture, so the picture does not show the 1 : 1.5 : 3 proportion by size.

belongs_to: Example 5: 'Construct a triangle with angles in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5' (triangle ABC drawn to the right of the working: angle A = 20°, B = 60°, C = 100°)
description: Single triangle ABC, drawn with blue outline and very light lavender-blue fill, a small blue dot at each vertex. A is the bottom-left vertex, B the bottom-right vertex, side AB is exactly horizontal and is the longest base; C is the top vertex, placed above and slightly left of B, so side AC is a long line rising to the right and side BC is a short steep line coming down to B. Vertex letters 'A' (left of A), 'B' (right of B), 'C' (above C) in dark serif text. Each of the three angles is marked by a small grey-filled circular sector with a thin blue arc at that vertex inside the triangle, with its degree label: '20°' written just above-right of A (above side AB, near the vertex), '60°' written just below-left of B (below side AB), '100°' written just to the right of C outside the triangle. The triangle is drawn to scale with these angles (angle at A about 20 degrees, at B about 60, at C about 100, obtuse). No side lengths are marked.

belongs_to: 3.5 'Now let us construct a pie chart using these angles' - Step 1: 'Draw a circle and mark the radius AB as shown below' and Step 2: 'measure 108° from the segment AB on A (anti-clockwise), and mark the new radius AC' (first row of the 7-step pie-chart construction; continues on page 8)
description: Pink-bordered box in two side-by-side panels (separated by a pink vertical line), each with its step text on top and a drawing below. PANEL 1 (Step 1): a plain black-outlined circle, no fill. The centre is a black dot labelled 'A' (label just left of the dot). A single black radius runs horizontally from A to the right end of the circle where a black dot labelled 'B' sits (label just right/inside of the dot). Nothing else. PANEL 2 (Step 2): the same circle; AB horizontal to the right as before ('A' label just left-below the centre, 'B' at the right end). A second radius AC runs from A up and slightly to the LEFT of vertical (108 degrees anti-clockwise from AB, i.e. 18 degrees past the upright) to a black dot on the circle labelled 'C' (above the dot). At A a small grey-filled circular sector with thin outline marks the angle between AB and AC; the label '108°' is written just above-right of A beside that sector. Circle in panel 2 is the same size as in panel 1.

belongs_to: 3.5 pie-chart construction, second row: 'Step 3: Measure 90° from AC and draw AD' and 'Step 4: Measure 72° from AD and draw AE' (continues from page 7)

All circles are plain black-outlined, no fill, centre A (black dot), radii as black lines, points as black dots with letters. PANEL STEP 3: circle with centre A. Radii: AB horizontal to the right (dot 'B' at the right end of the circle); AC rising up and slightly left of vertical (18 degrees past the upright, dot 'C' on the circle above); AD going down-left (dot 'D' on the circle at the lower left, 18 degrees below the left horizontal; label 'D' left of the dot). Letter 'A' is written just below the centre. PANEL STEP 4: same as step 3 plus a fourth radius AE going straight DOWN from A to a dot 'E' at the bottom of the circle (label 'E' below the dot). Markers: grey sector '108°' (upper right of A), grey right-angle square '90°' (left of A), and a new grey circular sector between AD and AE with label '72°' written below-left of A; label 'A' sits just below-right of the centre. The angle between AD and AE is 72 degrees (AD is 18 degrees below the left horizontal; AE is vertical).

belongs_to: 3.5 pie-chart construction, third and fourth panels: 'Steps 5,6: Similarly, we can complete the rest of the pie chart' and 'Step 7: You can colour and label the different slices of the pie chart appropriately' (continues from page 7; final row of the 2 x 2 box)
description: Bottom row of the pink-bordered 2 x 2 box: two side-by-side panels. PANEL STEPS 5,6: plain circle, no fill, centre A (black dot). Black radii and dots: AB horizontal to the right ('B'); AC up and slightly left of vertical ('C' above its dot); AD down-left ('D'); AE straight down ('E' below its dot); AF down-right, at 36 degrees below the horizontal AB (dot 'F' on the circle at the lower right, label 'F' below-right of the dot). Slice between AB and AC (upper right, 108 degrees) is filled green with the dark text 'Grade A'; slice between AC and AD (left, 90 degrees) is filled yellow with the text 'Grade B'; the other three slices (AD to AE at lower left, AE to AF at bottom right, AF to AB at right) are left white/unfilled and unlabelled. All slice borders are black lines.
unclear: In the Step 7 panel the three remaining slices (grades C, D, E) are blank in the book; they are not coloured or labelled.

belongs_to: 3.6 Figure it Out Q4: 'Fill in the average number of hours each living being sleeps in a day by looking at the charts. Select the appropriate hours from this list: 15, 2.5, 20, 8, 3.5, 13, 10.5, 18'
description: Grid of 8 donut (ring) charts, 2 rows of 4, same size, no title, no numbers, no key/legend, no captions. Each ring is split into two colours: ORANGE (amber, about #FDA81E) and INDIGO (blue-violet, about #4547A0); inside the white hole of every ring is a small coloured sketch of a sleeping living being. In every ring the INDIGO wedge starts at the 12 o'clock vertical radius and runs ANTI-CLOCKWISE (towards the left side), and the rest of the ring (clockwise from 12 o'clock) is orange. Measured share of the ring that is indigo (from pixel colour at mid-ring; about +/- 3 degrees), in book order: TOP ROW, left to right: (1) giraffe curled up asleep (spotted coat): indigo about 12% of the ring, about 43 degrees; (2) elephant curled up asleep (grey): indigo about 16%, about 56 degrees; (3) a child asleep with head on a pillow (dark hair, light green clothes): indigo about 33%, about 117 degrees; (4) a tan/brown dog lying on its back asleep: indigo about 42%, about 152 degrees. BOTTOM ROW, left to right: (5) grey tabby cat curled up asleep: indigo about 53%, about 191 degrees; (6) brown squirrel curled up: indigo about 62%, about 223 degrees; (7) green snake coiled: indigo about 75%, about 271 degrees; (8) brown bat hanging upside down, wings folded: indigo about 84%, about 302 degrees. The indigo share increases steadily from chart (1) to chart (8). The animals are not named in the text; the list of hours (15, 2.5, 20, 8, 3.5, 13, 10.5, 18) is printed above the grid.
unclear: No key is printed: that indigo means 'hours asleep' and orange 'hours awake' is inferred from the question and from the shares (indigo share x 24 hours = about 2.9, 3.7, 7.8, 10.2, 12.7, 14.9, 18.1, 20.1 hours, consistent with the list).
Wedge angles are measured from the scanned picture, not printed, so only approximate (+/- 3 degrees).
Identification of the animals (giraffe, elephant, child, dog, cat, squirrel, snake, bat) is from the sketches; chart (4) could also be read as another tan animal (dog assumed).

belongs_to: 3.6 Figure it Out Q5: 'The pie chart on the right shows the result of a survey carried out to find the modes of transport used by children to go to school. Study the pie chart and answer the following questions' (i)-(iv)
description: Black-outline pie chart (white fill, no colours, no title, no counts), top right of the page. Five slices separated by five radii from the centre: (1) a vertical radius pointing UP (12 o'clock); (2) a horizontal radius pointing LEFT (9 o'clock); (3) a radius pointing DOWN-LEFT (about 30 degrees to the left of straight down); (4) a vertical radius pointing DOWN (6 o'clock); (5) a radius pointing DOWN-RIGHT (about 30 degrees below the horizontal to the right, 4 o'clock). SLICES with their words printed inside (dark serif): upper-left quarter between radii (1) and (2): 'Walk'; upper-right big slice between radii (1) and (5): 'Bus'; bottom-right slice between radii (5) and (4): 'Two-' / 'wheeler' (hyphenated on two lines); narrow bottom slice between radii (4) and (3): 'Car'; left-lower slice between radii (3) and (2): 'Cycle'. ANGLE MARKS near the centre: '90°' with a small right-angle square mark in the Walk slice (label to the left of the square, just above the horizontal-left radius); '120°' with a small arc in the Bus slice (label right of the centre); '60°' with a small arc in the Cycle slice (label below the horizontal-left radius, left of radius (3)); '60°' with a small arc in the Two-wheeler slice (label below the centre, right of the vertical-down radius). So printed: Walk 90°, Bus 120°, Cycle 60°, Two-wheeler 60°; the Car slice carries NO angle label (it measures 30 degrees: 360 - 90 - 120 - 60 - 60).
unclear: The angle of the Car slice (30 degrees) is not printed; it is deduced from the others and agrees with the geometry of the picture (the radii measure about 30 degrees from the vertical).
Which of the two '60°' labels belongs to which slice is read from their position: the left one with Cycle, the lower-right one with Two-wheeler.
